# Notes.ThatVetGuy

> Free academic resources, thoughtfully made for future vets.

Notes.ThatVetGuy (Rx Notes by ThatVetGuy) is a free academic library for BVSc & AH students in India. Site summaries: Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. Notes and recommended reading are organised by professional year and subject. Topic notes open on Google Drive or their credited source PDFs and documents; objective and clinical collections open in Telegram. Book recommendations do not imply a downloadable copy is available. Known source credits are preserved; inclusion does not imply authorship or medical review.

Main website: https://thatvetguy.net
Author: Dr. Chirag Patidar
Last source review: 2026-10-28. File access settings can change.

---
Canonical: https://notes.thatvetguy.net/

# Veterinary Anatomy

Veterinary Anatomy focuses on relating structure to function across domestic animal species.

[Syllabus ChecklistUnit by unit. One tick at a time.](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/syllabus/)

# Livestock Production Management

Livestock Production Management focuses on connecting animal husbandry principles with practical farm management.

℞

## Notes

25 notes

#### Unit 1 General Livestock Management

1 notes

PDF
General Livestock Management[Open General Livestock Management](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1AGbIMXNivCW5o-pFaPm7rbKehpUBqnoN/view?usp=sharing)

#### Unit 2 Fodder Production and Conservation

# Veterinary Parasitology

Veterinary Parasitology focuses on understanding parasite life cycles and their significance in animal health.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/[BVSc](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/)/[1st Year](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/)/1st Year BVSc & AH Roadmap

# 1st Year Roadmap

Learn the normal. The abnormal can wait one year.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

Course-outline note. The uploaded 1st Year outline also includes Biochemistry and prints 21 credits. This guide uses the 18-credit MSVE professional-year distribution; Biochemistry is in 2nd Year here. Check your university's allocation.

## Year at a glance

- 18credits12 theory + 6 practical
- 3core coursesAnatomy · Physiology · LPM
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately
- 210teaching daysminimum; annual exam days excluded

- Use diagrams and specimens alongside theory; practical identification deserves its own revision time.
- Non-credit activities still need a satisfactory grade. Check your college's required programme.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 210 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Anatomy4 theory + 3 practical7 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/)
- [Physiology4 theory + 1 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/)
- [Livestock Production4 theory + 2 practical6 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/)

18 credits in total · 12 theory + 6 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Internal marks are your safety net.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Anatomy

Focus on Bones and joints; regional anatomy; histology and embryology.

Try this Learn a structure with its location, relations and function. Redraw it, then identify it on a specimen or slide.

A beautiful diagram with no labels is still an expensive doodle.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Physiology

Focus on Blood, cardiovascular and respiratory function; digestion; renal, endocrine and reproductive physiology.

Try this Explain each process as a sequence with feedback. Connect the practical observation to the mechanism it demonstrates.

If you cannot explain the feedback loop, rereading the arrow will not help.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/#notes)

3

### Livestock Production Management

Focus on Species-wise husbandry, housing, feeding management, handling and farm records.

Try this Compare species and life stages in a small table. Link each management practice to what you observe on the farm.

Do not leave LPM for the evening before the practical.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/livestock-production-management/#notes)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### After class

Close the notes and explain one process or redraw one labelled structure. Check what you missed.

- 

### After practicals

Finish observations while you remember the specimen, technique or farm visit.

- 

### At the weekend

Revisit older diagrams and one LPM comparison before planning the next week.

## Small habits, big saves

- Keep one main set of notes per subject; add corrections there instead of starting another notebook.
- Look at past professional papers for format and topic coverage, not a promise of repeated questions.
- Keep attendance and practical records up to date; they are not last-night tasks.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Map the course

Tick off theory units and practical competencies against your university outline.

- 

### Practise the format

Write timed answers with labelled diagrams; rehearse identification and viva explanations.

- 

### Repair weak spots

Use a short list of recurring mistakes, then revisit the original explanation.

Your skeleton has enough bones. Your folder does not need 47 versions.

Sources & academic notes

# 2nd Year Roadmap

Five subjects. Connect the dots, not five new notebooks.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

Course-outline note. Biochemistry appears in the uploaded 1st Year outline PDF. The MSVE professional-year distribution used here places it in 2nd Year.

## Year at a glance

- 22credits15 theory + 7 practical
- 5core coursesTheory and practical courses
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately
- 3 × 40internal marksthree scheduled tests; 40 marks each

- Connect Pathology and Microbiology, but keep regular slots for Genetics and Nutrition calculations.
- Finish practical records alongside the laboratory work; explain the observation, not just the result.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 210 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Pathology4 theory + 2 practical6 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/)
- [Microbiology3 theory + 2 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/)
- [Nutrition3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/)
- [Genetics & Breeding3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/)
- [Biochemistry2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/)

22 credits in total · 15 theory + 7 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Keep the number subjects warm all year.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Pathology

Focus on General and systemic pathology; oncology; clinical pathology and necropsy.

Try this Link cause, mechanism, gross lesion and microscopic change. Practise describing a lesion before naming a disease.

A disease name is not a lesion description.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-pathology/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Microbiology

Focus on Bacteriology, mycology, virology, immunology and microbial biotechnology.

Try this Compare organisms by transmission, pathogenesis and diagnostic approach. Revise laboratory identification with the related theory.

Organism names are not a substitute for understanding the test.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-microbiology/#notes)

3

### Animal Nutrition

Focus on Nutrients, feed evaluation, digestion and species-wise feeding principles.

Try this Work through ration and requirement examples with units shown. Explain the biological assumption behind each calculation.

The calculator cannot rescue the wrong units.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-nutrition/#notes)

4

### Animal Genetics and Breeding

Focus on Inheritance, population and quantitative genetics; selection and breeding systems.

Try this Write what each symbol means before using a formula. Solve fresh examples and check the interpretation, not only the number.

Memorising the formula is step one, not the whole personality.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/animal-genetics-and-breeding/#notes)

5

### Veterinary Biochemistry

Focus on Biomolecules, enzymes, metabolism, vitamins, minerals and biochemical methods.

Try this Map inputs, outputs and regulation of pathways. Connect biochemical tests to the principle being measured.

Do not turn a pathway into a list of unrelated reaction names.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/veterinary-biochemistry/#notes)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### Pair related topics

Study a pathogen with its lesions and the relevant laboratory method.

- 

### Keep numbers warm

Practise Genetics or Nutrition problems regularly, with working and units.

- 

### Close the loop

Review one lab observation and one older pathway without looking at the answer first.

## Small habits, big saves

- Use comparison tables only when they clarify a genuine distinction; avoid rewriting the whole textbook.
- Record why an answer was wrong: a concept gap, a missed fact, weak recall or an avoidable error.
- Keep the practical method, observation and interpretation together in your revision notes.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Separate the tasks

Make different checklists for descriptive answers, calculations and practical identification.

- 

### Practise mixed work

Alternate a calculation with a lesion or organism explanation to expose weak connections.

- 

### Revisit mistakes

Correct misunderstood concepts before repeatedly attempting the same question.

The syllabus is multiplying. At least your bacteria have an excuse.

# 3rd Year Roadmap

Now the earlier years start asking to be remembered.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

## Year at a glance

- 24credits15 theory + 9 practical
- 7core coursesTheory and practical courses
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately
- 3 × 40internal marksthree scheduled tests; 40 marks each

- Link the agent, disease process and prevention or treatment principle across subjects.
- Clinical Practices I and Livestock Farm Practices are practical courses; keep their records and assessment dates visible.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 210 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Pharmacology & Toxicology4 theory + 1 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/)
- [Parasitology3 theory + 2 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-parasitology/)
- [Public Health & Epidemiology3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/)
- [Extension Education3 theory + 1 practical4 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-and-animal-husbandry-extension-education/)
- [Livestock Products Tech2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-products-technology/)
- [Clinical Practices I0 theory + 1 practical1 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-clinical-practices-i/)
- [Livestock Farm Practices0 theory + 2 practical2 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-farm-practices/)

24 credits in total · 15 theory + 9 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Applied subjects reward practical understanding.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

Practical-only courses: VCC/LFC assessments follow a separate schedule at 50% and full course completion. Records, observed skills and viva preparation matter.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Pharmacology and Toxicology

Focus on General pharmacology; system-wise drugs; chemotherapy and toxicology.

Try this Organise each class by mechanism, uses, adverse effects and important cautions. Practise unit conversions from worked academic examples.

A brand name is not a mechanism of action.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-pharmacology-and-toxicology/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Parasitology

Focus on Helminths, arthropods and protozoa; identification, life cycles and diagnosis.

Try this Draw a life cycle with host, infective stage and diagnostic stage. Link each control principle to the point it interrupts.

Do not mix up the infective stage and the stage you identify.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-parasitology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-parasitology/#notes)

3

### Veterinary Public Health and Epidemiology

Focus on Zoonoses, food and environmental hygiene; epidemiological measures and investigations.

Try this Connect the source, transmission route and prevention. Work through epidemiology measures using the correct denominator.

The denominator is doing more work than the highlighter.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-public-health-and-epidemiology/#notes)

4

### Veterinary and Animal Husbandry Extension Education

Focus on Communication, extension methods, rural sociology, economics and entrepreneurship.

Try this Apply each method to a real livestock-owner situation. Practise explaining a technical message clearly in everyday language.

A perfectly memorised message still needs someone to understand it.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-and-animal-husbandry-extension-education/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-and-animal-husbandry-extension-education/#notes)

5

### Livestock Products Technology

Focus on Milk, meat and egg processing; product quality, preservation and abattoir practices.

Try this Make process flows with the purpose of each stage. Link a quality test to the property it assesses.

Learn why the process exists, not just the arrows between boxes.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-products-technology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-products-technology/#notes)

6

### Veterinary Clinical Practices I

Focus on Patient handling, clinical examination, case registration and diagnostic orientation.

Try this Observe a structured examination with your supervisor. Record findings, unfamiliar terms and the questions you need to ask.

A case log is more useful before the memory expires.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-clinical-practices-i/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/veterinary-clinical-practices-i/#notes)

7

### Livestock Farm Practices

Focus on Farm routines, animal records, feeding and management observations.

Try this Keep the day's farm activity and its purpose together. Ask for feedback on handling and record-keeping skills.

Farm records do not become easier when copied from memory in bulk.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-farm-practices/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/livestock-farm-practices/#notes)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### Connect three subjects

Use one example to link the disease process, causative agent and drug or prevention principle.

- 

### Make practicals count

Finish the case or farm record on the day and ask about one unclear step.

- 

### Revisit the foundations

Bring back relevant Physiology, Pathology or Microbiology when a new topic depends on it.

## Small habits, big saves

- Compress your own revision material after understanding a topic; a short note cannot replace a missing concept.
- Keep one error list and revisit it before the next practice session.
- Use professional exam papers for your university scheme; PG entrance questions have a different purpose.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Map every course

Include both practical-only courses, not just the five theory subjects.

- 

### Rehearse explanations

Practise a drug-class comparison, a parasite life cycle and an epidemiology problem.

- 

### Check practical readiness

Revisit identification, records and supervised skills as well as written answers.

Everything is connected. Unfortunately, so are your exam dates.

Sources & academic notes 

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

All seven courses are included below. Farm Practices contributes the final 2 practical credits, bringing the year to 24.

- Veterinary Council of India — MSVE Regulations, 2016Gazette, 12 July 2016: regulations 2, 11–13, 15–16; professional-year transcript in Annexure I.
- ICAR–Indian Veterinary Research Institute — Undergraduate ProgrammeSystem of education; professional-year course distribution; examinations.

Assessment coverage is cumulative: the 30%, 60% and 90% milestones are not guaranteed chapter ranges or predicted exam weightage.

Study suggestions are original editorial guidance based on the course topics and a reviewed first-person preparation account. No marks or rank are promised.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/[BVSc](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/)/[4th Year](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/)/4th Year BVSc & AH Roadmap

# 4th Year Roadmap

From knowing the answer to explaining your next step.

- [1Foundation](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)
- [2Disease & nutrition](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)
- [3Applied study](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)
- [4Clinical](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)
- [Internship](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/#internship)

MSVE 2016 · Syllabus & outline notes

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

## Year at a glance

- 17credits8 theory + 9 practical
- 4core coursesTheory and practical courses
- 1.5years18 months before the separate internship
- 50%to passtheory and practical, counted separately

- Bring Anatomy, Physiology, Pathology and Pharmacology into case-based reasoning.
- Clinical Practices II is a 0+6 practical course. Follow its clinical assessment and logbook requirements, not the theory-internal template.

Attendance: 75% minimum in theory and practical separately. 315 teaching days minimum, excluding annual exams.

## Where the credits go

Bigger bar, bigger commitment.

TheoryPractical

Tap a row to find its books and notes.

- [Medicine4 theory + 1 practical5 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-medicine/)
- [Surgery & Radiology2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-surgery-and-radiology/)
- [Gynaecology & Obstetrics2 theory + 1 practical3 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-gynaecology-and-obstetrics/)
- [Clinical Practices II0 theory + 6 practical6 credits](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-clinical-practices-ii/)

17 credits in total · 8 theory + 9 practical.

## Exam checkpoints

Practise the reasoning, not just the answer.

- 1

### Internal 1

By 30% course coverage

40 marks · close the first gaps
- 2

### Internal 2

By 60% course coverage

40 marks · connect the concepts
- 3

### Internal 3

By 90% course coverage

40 marks · revisit weak areas
- 4

### Annual exam

100% of the course

Full course · theory and practical

For theory-bearing subjects: three internals of 40 marks each; the best two assessments count under MSVE 2016. Use your university’s current dates and marking scheme.

Practical-only courses: VCC/LFC assessments follow a separate schedule at 50% and full course completion. Records, observed skills and viva preparation matter.

## Your subject playbook

Know what to learn. Know how to revise.

1

### Veterinary Medicine

Focus on Systemic and infectious diseases; diagnostic reasoning and preventive medicine.

Try this Present a case as history, findings, problem list and differentials. Explain which test would help distinguish them to your supervisor.

A list of diseases is not yet a differential diagnosis.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-medicine/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-medicine/#notes)

2

### Veterinary Surgery and Radiology

Focus on Surgical principles, anaesthesiology, imaging and regional surgery.

Try this Learn the indication and anatomical basis of a procedure with its preparation and aftercare. Practise permitted skills under supervision.

Knowing the instrument's name is the opening scene, not the whole surgery.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-surgery-and-radiology/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-surgery-and-radiology/#notes)

3

### Veterinary Gynaecology and Obstetrics

Focus on Reproduction, obstetrics, infertility and reproductive management.

Try this Link normal reproductive physiology to clinical findings. Compare species and practise structured case explanations.

Species differences have entered the chat.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-gynaecology-and-obstetrics/#books)[Topic-wise notes ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-gynaecology-and-obstetrics/#notes)

4

### Veterinary Clinical Practices II

Focus on Clinical rotations, case work, diagnostics and supervised clinical competencies.

Try this Keep a de-identified case log: what you observed, your reasoning, feedback and what you will review next.

The logbook is evidence of learning, not a scrapbook of signatures.

[Books & course outline ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/veterinary-clinical-practices-ii/#books)

## A week that works

Suggested rhythm. Adjust it to your timetable.

- 

### Before a posting

Review the examination approach and one relevant foundation topic.

- 

### After a case

Write a de-identified summary, check your reasoning and ask your supervisor for feedback.

- 

### Before the next week

Revisit unresolved questions and practical skills without letting written revision disappear.

## Small habits, big saves

- Explain why you chose an investigation or management principle; memorised lists alone do not show reasoning.
- Keep patient identifiers out of personal study notes and discuss cases within your institution's rules.
- Use current, species-appropriate references and supervisor guidance; a revision sheet is not a prescription.

Study advice, not an exam rule. A first-person account by Dr. Bhupender (AIEEA Animal Science 2022 Rank 1) informed the concise-revision and error-review habits; his PG strategy is not a professional-exam blueprint.

## Before the final stretch

- 

### Connect theory to cases

Practise concise problem lists, differentials and reasons for investigations.

- 

### Prepare both formats

Rehearse written answers and the practical examination or viva separately.

- 

### Prepare for internship

Check completion of credits, records and university instructions for rotating postings.

The patient did not read your predicted questions.

## Next stop: internship

After passing the fourth professional and completing the required credits, the MSVE 2016 programme includes a separate compulsory 12-month rotating internship.

Follow your university’s posting schedule, supervision, logbook and completion requirements. Clinical Practices II is part of the fourth professional; it is not the internship.

Sources & academic notes 

An MSVE 2016 study guide. Your university's current syllabus, assessment scheme and academic calendar take precedence.

The fourth professional spans 18 months under MSVE 2016, followed by a separate compulsory 12-month rotating internship.

- Veterinary Council of India — MSVE Regulations, 2016Gazette, 12 July 2016: regulations 2, 11–13, 15–16; professional-year transcript in Annexure I.
- ICAR–Indian Veterinary Research Institute — Undergraduate ProgrammeSystem of education; professional-year course distribution; examinations.

Assessment coverage is cumulative: the 30%, 60% and 90% milestones are not guaranteed chapter ranges or predicted exam weightage.

Study suggestions are original editorial guidance based on the course topics and a reviewed first-person preparation account. No marks or rank are promised.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/Tips & Tools for Vet Study

# Tips & Tools for Vet Study

Explore practical AI study guidance, useful free apps and everyday study tools for veterinary students. Use the guides to organise reading, references and presentations while checking veterinary information against trusted sources.

[Tools](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#tools)[Tips](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/study-tools/#tips)

## Use of AI for Vet Study

- 

### Start with your outline

Ask AI to organise a topic list or suggest a presentation structure. Compare the result with your syllabus and original notes.

- 

### Check before you learn

Verify veterinary facts and citations. A fluent answer can still be wrong; AI output is not a prescribing reference.

- 

### Make the explanation yours

Explain the topic without looking at the answer. Rewrite it in your own words and credit your sources.

## Useful Free Apps

- 

### Zotero

Keep reading references together. Check each citation against its original source.

- 

### LibreOffice

Prepare notes, tables and presentations. Keep an editable copy as well as a PDF.

- 

### Your PDF reader

Use bookmarks, annotations and text search. Keep essential reading in a clearly named offline folder.

## Useful Study Tools

- 

### A document scanner

Scan only material you have permission to copy. Check every page for legibility before sharing.

- 

### A simple folder system

Try Year / Subject / Notes or Books. A useful filename saves a surprising amount of searching.

- 

### A reference checklist

Record the author, edition, species and date where relevant. A saved file still needs context.

## Year Roadmaps

[1st Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/roadmap/)[2nd Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-2/roadmap/)[3rd Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-3/roadmap/)[4th Year Roadmap](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-4/roadmap/)

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/About Notes.ThatVetGuy

# About Notes.ThatVetGuy

Notes.ThatVetGuy is a free academic library for BVSc & AH students. Find notes, books and practical material by year, with study guides to help you choose what to read next.

## A useful place to start.

Pick your professional year, find a subject and get to the reading. Notes.ThatVetGuy brings notes, books and practical material together for veterinary students.

## People behind the pages

Site guidance and summaries are by Dr. Chirag Patidar, BVSc & AH, MVSc. Linked materials retain their original authorship. Inclusion does not imply medical review or ownership.

## Help the next student

A missing topic, a broken file or a credit that needs correcting: tell us so the library can get better.

[Request or report a resource ](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/request-resource/)

## Questions, answered

Where do resources open?

Topic-wise notes open on Google Drive. Objective notes, question banks, drug references and handbooks open in Telegram; some collections require access. Recommended books do not always have a linked copy. Original authors retain credit.

Does the year grouping match my syllabus?

Year grouping may vary by university. Check your syllabus before planning revision.

Page updated: 2026-10-20. Sources last reviewed: 2026-10-28; external file availability can change.

# Can’t find what you need?

Request a veterinary note, book, PYQ or useful study resource, or report a link that needs attention. Include the subject, year and source so the library can be improved for other veterinary students.

↳ Can't find it? Ask. The library has an excellent memory.

## Tell us what would help.

Include the topic, subject, year and edition if relevant.

File ID, if reporting a file

[Email your request ](mailto:contact@thatvetguy.net?subject=Resource%20request)

You can also copy contact@thatvetguy.net into your email app.

## Contact

Send your question to contact@thatvetguy.net.

## Contribute

Send the title, subject and original source credit. Share only material you have permission to contribute.

## Report an error / takedown

Include the file ID or page URL, the issue and your contact details. For a takedown request, explain your connection to the material.

## Questions, answered

How do I report a broken link?

Email contact@thatvetguy.net with the page URL and resource name. The visible email address can be copied if your email application does not open.

Can I contribute a resource?

Send the original source, title and subject to contact@thatvetguy.net. Share material you have permission to contribute.

# Drug Index Collection

Veterinary drug indexes, a drug handbook, a wall reference and vaccination schedules in one collection. Choose a resource to see its details and Telegram download link. Check the edition before clinical use.

For study, not prescribing. Verify the species, dose and current clinical guidance before treating a patient.

## About this book

Applied Nutrition: Livestock, Poultry, Rabbits and Laboratory Animals is a nutrition text by D. V. Reddy. The source title page identifies this copy as the third edition. It is filed in the Animal Nutrition Books collection for second-year BVSc & AH reading. Use your course outline to select the relevant species and nutrition themes, and keep this applied text distinct from Principles of Animal Nutrition and Feed Technology.

# Drug Dose — Wall Reference

[Download via Telegram](https://t.me/c/4430259212/7)

This button opens the book’s Telegram post. View or download the file there. This is a private collection; access to its posts is required.

## About this reference

A printable quick-reference sheet; verify every dose against current clinical guidance.

For study and supervised reference. Verify the species, dose, edition and current clinical guidance before treating a patient.

## A study note

Use this as a reference to look up a specific question, rather than a substitute for current clinical guidance. Confirm the edition, species and context before relying on a table or recommendation.

# Essentials of Veterinary Histology & Embryology

R. K. Ghosh

[Download via Telegram](https://t.me/c/4312433672/3)

This button opens the book’s Telegram post. View or download the file there. This is a private collection; access to its posts is required.

## About this book

R. K. Ghosh’s text brings microscopic anatomy and embryology together for veterinary study. Use it to connect normal tissue structure with organ function, then follow development from fertilisation to birth. It is useful alongside slide identification and embryology lectures. Check the linked copy’s title page and edition before planning your reading.

# Plumb’s Veterinary Drug Handbook

Donald C. Plumb

[Download via Telegram](https://t.me/c/4430259212/5)

This button opens the book’s Telegram post. View or download the file there. This is a private collection; access to its posts is required.

## About this book

Plumb’s Veterinary Drug Handbook is a veterinary drug reference organised around individual medicines. It brings together information used to look up veterinary drug monographs, including precautions and interactions. It is a reference for trained clinical use, not a substitute for diagnosis or current product information. Confirm the edition of the linked copy and use current, species-specific clinical guidance.

For study and supervised reference. Verify the species, dose, edition and current clinical guidance before treating a patient.

## A study note

## About this book

Primary Veterinary Anatomy introduces gross anatomy for veterinary students. R. K. Ghosh’s text relates the arrangement of organs and body regions to dissection, with comparative material across domestic animals and birds. Use it to build anatomical terminology, identify structures in practical classes and connect systems with their position and relationships. Stephen J. Ettinger

[Open in Google Drive](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1mr1sLm0C53nUKO_YKiOV80nXeUzCoVcu/view)

View or download this copy in Google Drive. Check its title page and edition before use.

## About this book

Textbook of Veterinary Internal Medicine is listed in the Veterinary Medicine Books collection for Year 4 BVSc & AH study. Use it alongside your course outline and teaching notes, and check the linked copy’s title page and edition before citing it.

For study and supervised reference. Verify the species, dose, edition and current clinical guidance before treating a patient.

Use this alongside veterinary medicine lectures and practicals. Start with the topics in your current unit, then test whether you can explain the key ideas without the page in front of you.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/[BVSc](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/)/[1st Year](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/)/[Veterinary Anatomy](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-anatomy/)/Veterinary Anatomy Syllabus Checklist

# Veterinary Anatomy Syllabus Checklist

Your 1st Year course outline, one topic at a time. Tick what you have covered and pick up where you left off.

0 of 127 topics checked0%

Your progress stays on this device.

You can tick topics here. Enable JavaScript to save progress between visits.

[Theory](#theory)[Practical](#practical)

## Theory

### Unit 1General Anatomy

0 / 17

- [ ] Introduction to anatomy and branches of anatomy and descriptive terms used in anatomy and study of anatomical planes.
- [ ] General Osteology, Arthrology and Myology: Study of properties and structure of bone.
- [ ] Classification of skeletons, classification of bones with suitable examples and terms used in osteology Introduction to arthrology, classification of joints, different diarthrodial joints, structure of diarthrodial joints and movements permitted.
- [ ] Introduction to myology, classification of muscles, etymology of muscles.
- [ ] Description of tendon, ligaments, aponeurosis, synovial bursa and synovial sheath.
- [ ] (Note: Detailed description of muscles of different regions of the body will be studied in the respective practical).
- [ ] General Angiology, Neurology and Aesthesiology: Introduction to angiology.
- [ ] Structure of heart.
- [ ] General plan of systemic and pulmonary circulations, lymphatic and venous systems.
- [ ] Introduction to neurology and parts of central, peripheral and autonomic nervous system and sense organs.
- [ ] Formation of spinal nerve.
- [ ] Structure of meninges, brain, spinal cord.
- [ ] Different surface regions, joint regions, Palpable Bony areas or prominences of the body of the animal.
- [ ] Palpable Lymph nodes and Arteries of the body and Surface veins for Venepuncture.
- [ ] Sites for collection of Bone marrow and Cerebrospinal fluid.
- [ ] General Splanchnology: Introduction to splanchnology, boundaries of thoracic, abdominal and pelvic cavities, topography of different organs of digestive, respiratory, urinary, endocrine, male and female reproductive systems of domestic animals and fowl.
- [ ] Principles and application of Radiography and Ultrasound for bones and soft tissues.

### Unit 2Fore Limb

0 / 4

- [ ] Fore limb: Study of bones of fore limb of ox and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of hoof of ox and horse.
- [ ] Study of joints, ligaments, stay apparatus, major blood vessels, nerves, veins and lymph nodes of fore limb.
- [ ] Sites for Radial, Median, Ulnar and Volar nerve blocks.

### Unit 3Head and Neck

0 / 12

- [ ] Head and neck: Study of cranial and facial bones, cervical vertebrae of ox and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Boundaries of the oral, orbital, nasal and cranial cavities.
- [ ] Study of paranasal sinuses in ox, horse, dog and pig.
- [ ] Study of articulations and special ligaments of the head and neck.
- [ ] Muscles of face, mastication, eye, ear, tongue, pharynx, soft palate ,hyoid and larynx.
- [ ] Study of teeth, hard and soft palate, tongue, pharynx, larynx, thyroid, parathyroid and salivary glands and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of cranial nerves, blood vessels and lymph nodes of head and neck regions.
- [ ] Study of boundaries of jugular furrow and structures of carotid sheath along with neck muscles.
- [ ] Study of sense organs, trachea and oesophagus.
- [ ] Age determination by Dentition.
- [ ] Sites for Tracheotomy, Esophagotomy, Ligation of Stensons duct and Mental, Mandibular, Maxillary , Cornual, Infraorabital , Supraorbital (frontal) , Orbital and Auriculopalpebral nerve blocks and surgical approach to guttural pouches in horse.
- [ ] Importance of Cornual nerve and superficial Temporal artery in Amputation of Horn in cattle.

### Unit 4Thorax

0 / 5

- [ ] Thorax: Study of thoracic vertebrae, ribs and sternum of ox and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of joints, special ligaments, blood vessels, nerves, lymph vessels and lymph nodes of thorax.
- [ ] Study of organs of thorax i.e. trachea, thymus, oesophagus, lungs and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of pleura, its reflections and mediastinum.
- [ ] Areas of auscultation and percussion of heart and lungs and site for Paracentesis Thoracis.

### Unit 5Abdomen

0 / 9

- [ ] Abdomen: Study of bones of abdomen of ox and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of joints, special ligaments blood vessels, nerves of abdomen region.
- [ ] Blood and nerve supply to abdominal viscera.
- [ ] Study of peritoneal reflections, organs of digestive, urinary, male and female reproductive systems present in abdomen and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of mammary glands in cow and differences in mare, bitch and sow.
- [ ] Study of spleen of ox and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of major veins, lymph vessels, lymph nodes and endocrine glands of abdomen.
- [ ] Boundaries and Clinical importance of the flank and Para Lumbar Fossa.
- [ ] Sites for Liver ,Gall Bladder and Caecal Biopsies, Laparotomy,Rumenocentesis ,Rumenotomy,abomasotomy, spleenectomy, Cystotomy , Caesarean Operation , enterotomy, and paravertebral block .

### Unit 6Hind Limb and Pelvis

0 / 6

- [ ] Hind limb and pelvis: Study of bones of hind limb and pelvis of ox and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of joints, ligaments, blood vessels, lymph nodes and nerves of hind limb, pelvis and tail region and pelvic viscera.
- [ ] Study of pelvic peritoneal reflections, organs of digestive, urinary, male and female reproductive systems present in pelvic cavity and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Boundaries of the inguinal canal and structures of the spermatic cord, pre pubic tendon and its importance.
- [ ] Study of external genital organs.
- [ ] Sites for Tibial , Peroneal ,Plantar and Pudic nerve blocks, Patellar desmotomy, Urethrotomy, Castration , Vasectomy, cranial and caudal epidural anaesthesia.

### Unit 7Cytology and Microscopic Anatomy

0 / 3

- [ ] Cytology, cell junctions, study of basic tissues i.e epithelial, connective, muscular and nervous tissues, blood and bone marrow.
- [ ] Study of microscopic structures of digestive, circulatory, urinary, respiratory, nervous, lymphatic, endocrine, male and female genital systems and mammary glands of domestic animals.
- [ ] Study of microscopic structure of sense organs i.e. eye, ear and integument.

### Unit 8Embryology

0 / 6

- [ ] Introduction to embryology, gametogenesis, fertilization, cleavage, types of eggs, morula, blastulation, gastrulation, types of implantation, twinning.
- [ ] Formation of foetal membranes in mammals and birds, Placenta and its classification.
- [ ] Different germ layers and their derivatives.
- [ ] Study of development of organs of digestive system including accessory structures i.e tongue, teeth, salivary glands, liver and pancreas.
- [ ] Study of development of organs of respiratory, urinary, circulatory, lymphatic, nervous, musculoskeletal, male and female reproductive systems.
- [ ] Development of endocrine glands, sense organs i.e eye and ear.

## Practical

### Unit 1General Anatomy

0 / 8

- [ ] Study of general terms used in anatomy, study of anatomical planes.
- [ ] Study of different parts of skeleton, different surface and joint regions.
- [ ] Study of boundaries of thoracic, abdominal and pelvic cavities.
- [ ] Demonstration of different types of joints, muscles tendons, ligaments, synovial bursa and synovial sheath.
- [ ] In situ demonstration of heart, meninges, brain and spinal cord.
- [ ] Boundaries of Thoracic, Abdominal and Pelvic Cavities and in situ demonstration of organs of digestive, respiratory, urinary, endocrine, male and female reproductive systems of domestic animals.
- [ ] Demonstration of Different surface regions, joint regions and Palpable Bony areas or prominences of the body of the animal , Common sites of fractures, Palpable Lymph nodes and Arteries of the body ( ventral coccygeal artery in ox, femoral artery in dog and cat , facial artery in horse ) and Surface veins for Venepuncture( cephalic vein and recurrent tarsal vein in dog and cat , jugular vein in large animals.) and Sites for collection of Bone marrow and Cerebrospinal fluid.
- [ ] Visualization of Radiographs and ultrasound pictures of various organs and Fractures of various bones.

### Unit 2Fore Limb

0 / 8

- [ ] Fore limb: Demonstration of different bones of fore limb of ox and comparison with horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Dissection of the fore limb.
- [ ] Study of joints, ligaments, muscles, major blood vessels, lymph nodes and nerves of fore limb.
- [ ] Study of sites for different nerves blocksorneurectomies in fore-limb.
- [ ] Study of suprascapular nerve paralysis-shoulder sweeny, radial nerve paralysis-capped elbow.
- [ ] Structure of the equine hoof and comparison with ox.
- [ ] Demonstration of radiographs of normal bones of fore limb.
- [ ] Clinical importance of cephalic vein for intravenous injections in dog.

### Unit 3Head and Neck

0 / 14

- [ ] Head and neck: Demonstration of cranial and facial bones, cervical vertebrae of ox and comparison with horse, dog and fowl.
- [ ] Dissection of muscles of face, mastication, tongue, pharynx, soft palate, hyoid, larynx, eye and ear.
- [ ] Dissection of superficial neck muscles.
- [ ] Dissection of brain and its parts.
- [ ] Dissectionordemonstration of tunics of eye.
- [ ] Study of teeth, tongue, pharynx, thyroid, parathyroid and salivary glands and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of cranial nerves, and blood vessels of head and neck regions.
- [ ] Study of trachea and oesophagus.
- [ ] Study of nerve blocks of the head i.e cornual, auriculo-palpebral, Peterson’s orbital nerve block, mandibulo-alveolar and mental nerve blocks.
- [ ] Importance of facial artery for recording pulse in horse.
- [ ] Surgical importance of Stenson’s duct in domestic animals.
- [ ] Surgical approach to guttural pouches-Viborg’s triangle.
- [ ] Clinical importance of jugular vein for intravenous injections in large animals.
- [ ] Demonstration of radiographs of normal bones of head and neck.

### Unit 4Thorax

0 / 8

- [ ] Thorax: Demonstration of thoracic vertebrae, ribs and sternum of ox and comparison with horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Dissection of muscles, blood vessels, nerves and lymph nodes of thorax.
- [ ] Demonstration of organs of thorax i.e. trachea, oesophagus, thymus, lungs and heart and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of pleural reflections of thoracic cavity.
- [ ] Demonstration of sites for auscultation and percussion.
- [ ] Recurrent laryngeal nerve paralysis-roaring in horses.
- [ ] Choke or oesophageal obstruction.
- [ ] Demonstration of radiographs and videos of ultrasonography of organs of thorax.

### Unit 5Abdomen

0 / 9

- [ ] Abdomen: Demonstration of bones forming boundaries of abdomen of ox and comparison with horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Dissection of muscles, blood vessels and nerves of abdomen.
- [ ] Demonstration of peritoneum, omentum, mesentry and organs of digestive, urinary, male and female reproductive systems present in abdomen and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Demonstration of mammary glands of cow, mare, bitch and sow.
- [ ] Demonstration of major veins, lymph vessels and lymph nodes of abdomen.
- [ ] Topographic location of abdominal viscera of ox and comparison with horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Demonstration of sites for laparotomy, caesarean section, ovario-hysterectomy, catheterization of urinary bladder and sites for paravertebral and epidural anaesthesia.
- [ ] Demonstration of Boundaries and Clinical importance of the flank and Para Lumbar Fossa,Sites for Liver ,Gall Bladder and Caecal Biopsies, Laparotomy,Rumenocentesis ,Rumenotomy,abomasotomy, spleenectomy Cystotomy , Caesarean Operation, catheterization of urinary bladder and enterotomy and paravertebral block .
- [ ] Demonstration of radiographs and videos of ultrasonography of organs of abdomen.

### Unit 6Hind Limb and Pelvis

0 / 9

- [ ] Hind limb and pelvis: Demonstration of bones of hind limb of ox and comparison with horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Demonstration of joints and ligaments of hind limb and pelvis.
- [ ] Dissection of muscles, blood vessels, lymph nodes and nerves of hind limb and pelvic cavity.
- [ ] Demonstration of peritoneal reflections of pelvic cavity and organs of digestive, urinary, male and female reproductive systems in pelvic cavity and differences in horse, dog, pig and fowl.
- [ ] Study of external genital organs.
- [ ] Clinical importance of femoral artery to record pulse in dog.
- [ ] Clinical importance of recurrent tarsal vein for intravenous injections in dog.
- [ ] Demonstration of radiographs of normal bones and videos of ultrasonography of organs of pelvis.
- [ ] Demonstration of Sites for Tibial ,Peroneal ,Plantar and Pudic nerve blocks, Patellar desmotomy, Urethrotomy, Castration , Vasectomy and cranial and caudal epidural anaesthesia.

### Unit 7Cytology and Microscopic Anatomy

0 / 5

- [ ] Microscopy and micrometry.
- [ ] Comparison of light and electron microscopy.
- [ ] Histological techniques, processing of tissues for paraffin sectioning and haematoxylin and eosin staining.
- [ ] Microscopic examination of epithelium, connective tissue, muscular tissue, nervous tissue and blood.
- [ ] Microscopic examination of organs of digestive, circulatory, urinary, respiratory, nervous, lymphatic, endocrine, male and female genital systems and sensory organs of domestic animals.

### Unit 8Embryology

0 / 4

- [ ] Demonstration of Placenta, umbilical cord and foetal membranes of different domestic animals.
- [ ] Demonstration of congenital anomalies of domestic animals as per availability.
- [ ] Study of slides of developing organs of different systems as per the availability.
- [ ] A embalmed cadaver of buffalo calf (procured through donated animals or cadevars obtained from post-mortem section) for every 24 students to be used for dissection purposes.

[Home](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/)/[BVSc](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/)/[1st Year](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/)/[Veterinary Physiology](https://notes.thatvetguy.net/bvsc/year-1/veterinary-physiology/)/Veterinary Physiology Syllabus Checklist

# Veterinary Physiology Syllabus Checklist

Your 1st Year course outline, one topic at a time. Tick what you have covered and pick up where you left off.

0 of 93 topics checked0%

Your progress stays on this device.

You can tick topics here. Enable JavaScript to save progress between visits.

[Theory](#theory)[Practical](#practical)

## Theory

### Unit 1Blood, Cardiovascular, Nervous And Muscular Systems

0 / 26

- [ ] Introduction to Blood
- [ ] Properties of blood as a body fluid, metabolism and fate of R.B.C
- [ ] Hemoglobin-chemical structure, synthesis, physiological functions, derivatives of hemoglobin
- [ ] Heart- morphological characteristic, systemic excitability conduction and transmission processes.
- [ ] Cardiac Cycle: Regulation of cardiac output
- [ ] coronary circulation
- [ ] properties of pulse
- [ ] metabolism and energetic of working myocardial cell, extrinsic and intrinsic regulation
- [ ] Electro Cardio Graph and its significance in Veterinary Sciences -Echocardiography.
- [ ] Haemorrhage haemostasis.
- [ ] Haemodynamics of circulation, circulatory mechanics, resistance to flow, vasoconstriction, nervous and circulating fluid volume controls of blood pressure, neurohormonal control of vascular smooth muscle.
- [ ] Circulatory controls- shock stresses, regional and fetal circulation.
- [ ] Capillary exchange, control of blood pressure.
- [ ] Adjustment of circulation during exercise.
- [ ] Muscle Physiology-basic muscle unit characteristic-electrical phenomenon in muscle cell - muscle action potential, excitation and propagation of impulse characteristics- latent period refractive ness, threshold level-all and none characteristics - contractile mechanism - excitation - contraction coupling-neuro-muscular transmission, types of muscle contraction, phenomenon of fatigue, rigor mortis.
- [ ] Organization of nervous system- Mechanism of information processing, hierarchical control.
- [ ] Major function system- sensory, consciousness, emotion, motor and visceral control and basic functional unit - neuron structure, type- functional characteristics of sub-units of neuron.
- [ ] Membrane potential -ionic basis of resting membrane potential (RMP) nerve action potential, excitation and propagation of impulse characteristics- latent period- refractive-ness, threshold level-all and none characteristics.
- [ ] Degeneration and regeneration of nerve fibre.
- [ ] Synaptic and junctional transmission.
- [ ] Functions of nervous system-reflexes-control of posture and movements, autonomic nervous system and visceral control.
- [ ] Neurotransmitter wakefulness, sleep cycle.
- [ ] Higher function of neurons system - learning, memory, electroencephalography.
- [ ] Sense organs and receptors physiology of special senses - Eye: functional morphology, nourishment and protection neural pathway, receptors- optics, ocular muscles and movements, photochemistry, Vision defects Ear: Physiology of hearing and common hearing impairment.
- [ ] Vestibule apparatus.
- [ ] Physiology of olfaction and taste

### Unit 2Digestive And Respiratory Systems

0 / 15

- [ ] Morphological characteristic of mono gastric and poly gastric digestive system.
- [ ] Prehension, rumination
- [ ] defecation
- [ ] vomition
- [ ] regulation of secretory function of saliva, stomach, intestine, pancreas
- [ ] bile secretion
- [ ] hunger, appetite control, developmental aspects of digestion
- [ ] luminous, membranous and microbial digestion in rumen and intestine
- [ ] permeability characteristics of intestine, forces governing absorption, control intestinal transport of electrolyte and water, enzymatic digestion in monogastric and fermentative digestion in rumen, modification of toxic substances in rumen.
- [ ] Digestion in birds.
- [ ] Functional morphology of respiratory apparatus.
- [ ] Mechanics of breathing.
- [ ] Transport of blood gases, foetal and neonatal oxygen transport, dissociation curves, pressures, recoil tendency, elasticity, surfactants, pleural liquid, compliance, exchanges of gases in lungs and tissues, neural and chemical regulation of breathing, diffusion, perfusion, hypoxia.
- [ ] Frictional resistance to air flow, airways smooth muscle contraction, respiratory muscle work, panting, adaptation of respiration during muscle exercise, high altitude hypoxia, Non-respiratory lung functions.
- [ ] Respiration in birds.

### Unit 3Excretory And Endocrine Systems

0 / 13

- [ ] Kidney- Functional morphology of nephrons, factors determining filtration pressure, determination of glomerular filtration rate (GFR) and renal plasma flow — Re-absorption mechanisms for glucose, protein, amino acids, electrolytes
- [ ] ammonium mechanism, glomerulo-tubular balance, methods of studying renal functions
- [ ] urine concentration
- [ ] micturition, uremia.
- [ ] Fluid, water balance, fluid therapy, dehydration, water concentration mechanisms.
- [ ] Acid base balance and H+ regulation, correction and evolution of imbalances, total osmotic pressure.
- [ ] Formation and excretion of urine of Birds.
- [ ] Cerebrospinal fluid, synovial fluids - composition, formation and flow
- [ ] Joints.
- [ ] Regulation of bone metabolism and homeostasis.
- [ ] Hormone cell interaction, sub-cellular mechanisms-metabolism of hormones-methods of study of endocrine system
- [ ] Receptors- mechanism of regulation
- [ ] Chemistry of hypothalamo- hypophyseal hormones, target organ, pineal, thyroid, thymus, pancreas, adrenal, prostaglandins, hormones of calcium metabolism, disorders, rennin-angiotensin system, atrial natriuretic factors, erythropoietin, GI hormones, pheromones.

### Unit 4Reproduction, Lactation, Growth And Environmental Physiology

0 / 20

- [ ] Genetic and endocrine control of gonadal development, modification of gonadotrophin release, ovarian functions, follicular development, dynamics, endocrine and receptor profiles, sexual receptivity, ovarian cycle, post-partum ovarian activity, ovum transport, capacitation, fertilization, reproductive cycles in farm animals- hormones present in the biological fluids during pregnancy and their uses for the diagnosis of pregnancy- maternal foetal placental participation in pregnancy and parturition, immunology of gestation, preparturient endocrine status.
- [ ] Spermatogenic cycle and wave- function of sertoli cell-leydig cell-semen - composition- evaluation
- [ ] Testosterone -function and regulation - cryptorchidism.
- [ ] Puberty - photoperiod - uses of androgens, progestogens, estrogens.
- [ ] Functional and metabolic organization of mammary glands - structure and development
- [ ] effect of estrogens and progesterone
- [ ] hormonal control of mammary growth
- [ ] lactogenesis and galctogenesis
- [ ] biosynthesis of milk constituents-secretion of milk, and metabolism, prolactin and lactation cycle.
- [ ] Biochemical and genetic determinants of growth, regulation of growth, metabolic and hormone interactions, factors affecting efficiency of growth and production in ruminants and single stomach animals.
- [ ] Growth in meat producing animals and birds, growth curves.
- [ ] Recombinant gene transfer technologies for growth manipulation- advantages and limitations.
- [ ] Protein deposition in animals and poultry.
- [ ] Heat balance, heat tolerance, hypothermia, hyperthermia, thermo-regulation in farm animals, role of skin, responses of animals to heat and cold, fever, body temperature and hibernation.
- [ ] Temperature regulation in birds.
- [ ] Climatology- various parameters and their importance.
- [ ] Effect of different environmental variables like temperature, humidity, light, radiation, altitude on animal performance.
- [ ] Acclimation, acclimatization - general adaptive syndrome.
- [ ] Clinical aspects of endocrine - reproductive functions, circadian rhythm.
- [ ] Neurophysiology of behaviours, types of behaviour, communication, Learning and memory behavioural plasticity.

## Practical

### Unit 1Blood, Cardiovascular, Nervous And Muscular Systems

0 / 2

- [ ] Collection of blood samples - Separation of serum and plasma - Preservation of de-fribrinated blood - enumeration of erythrocytes, leucocytes - differential leucocytic count - platelet count - estimation of hemoglobin - haematocrit -erythrocyte sedimentation rate - packed cell volume - coagulation time- bleeding time -Erythrocyte fragility and viscosity - blood grouping - recording of ECG - measurement of arterial blood pressure (Sphygmomanometry).
- [ ] Simulation experiments on Nerve- Muscle and heart physiology.

### Unit 2Digestive And Respiratory Systems

0 / 5

- [ ] Counting of rumen motility, estimation of volatile fatty acids and ammonia nitrogen in rumen liquor.
- [ ] Bacterial and protozoal count.
- [ ] In-vitro action of proteolytic enzymes- Amylase, pepsin and trypsin.
- [ ] Recording of respiration, spirometry.
- [ ] Recording of volume and capacities in different physiological states including determination of vital capacities.

### Unit 3Excretory And Endocrine Systems

0 / 4

- [ ] Urine analysis-physiological constituents, pathological determinates, determination of Glomerular Filteration Rate.
- [ ] Titerable acidity, determination of inorganic phosphorus, urine ammonia nitrogen and creatinine in urine.
- [ ] Recording of rumenorintestinal movements (Demonstration) and Bio assay for tropic hormone.
- [ ] Demonstration of hormone estimation.

### Unit 4Reproduction, Lactation, Growth And Environmental Physiology

0 / 8

- [ ] Oestrus and phases of oestrous cycle in animals (vaginal mucus).
- [ ] Behavioural signs of oestrus.
- [ ] Sperm motility, sperm concentration -live and dead - abnormal sperm count.
- [ ] Measurement of growth in various species.
- [ ] Measuring surface area of animals.
- [ ] Health parameters of animals- body temperature, pulse, respiration and heart rate.
- [ ] Measurement of animal environmental conditions.
- [ ] Behaviour of animals- mating behavior, feeding behaviour (liveorvideo graphicorcomputer simulated demonstration).

# Livestock Production Management Syllabus Checklist

Your 1st Year course outline, one topic at a time. Tick what you have covered and pick up where you left off.

0 of 229 topics checked0%

Your progress stays on this device.

You can tick topics here. Enable JavaScript to save progress between visits.

[Theory](#theory)[Practical](#practical)

## Theory

### Unit 1General Livestock Management

0 / 15

- [ ] Demographic distribution of livestock and role in Indian economy.
- [ ] Problems and prospects of livestock industry in India.
- [ ] Common animal husbandry terms.
- [ ] (glossary) Body conformation and identification.
- [ ] Transportation of livestock and wild or zoo animals.
- [ ] Common farm management practices including disinfection, isolation, quarantine and disposal of carcass.
- [ ] Introduction to methods of drug administration.
- [ ] Common vices of animals (Cattle, Buffalo, Sheep, Goat,), their prevention and care.
- [ ] Livestock production systems.
- [ ] Animal holding and land holding patterns in different agro-climatic zones.
- [ ] Organic livestock production.
- [ ] Judging and BCS for body parts of livestock.
- [ ] Preparation of animals for show.
- [ ] Culling of animals.
- [ ] Selection and purchase of livestock.

### Unit 2Fodder Production And Conservation

0 / 8

- [ ] Importance of grasslands and fodder in livestock production.
- [ ] Agronomical Practices for fodder production.
- [ ] Important leguminous and non-leguminous fodders in different seasons.
- [ ] Soil and Water conservation and drainage of water for fodder production.
- [ ] Fodder production for small livestock units.
- [ ] Structures for storage of feeds and fodders.
- [ ] Scarcity fodders and preservation of green fodder.
- [ ] Recycling of animal washings and wastes in fodders production and use of recycle waste.

### Unit 3Livestock Production Management-Ruminants

0 / 21

- [ ] Housing systems, layout and design of different buildings for animals.
- [ ] Selection of site.
- [ ] General principles affecting the design and construction of building for housing for various livestock species.
- [ ] Arrangements of the building with special reference to Indian conditions.
- [ ] Utilization of local materials.
- [ ] Building materials used for construction of wall, roof and floor of animal houses, their characteristics, merits and demerits.
- [ ] Breeds of cattle and buffalo and descriptions of important breeds.
- [ ] Economic traits of cattle and buffaloes.
- [ ] General management and feeding practices of calves, heifers, pregnant, lactating and dry animals, bulls and working animals.
- [ ] Draught ability of cattle and buffaloes.
- [ ] Raising of buffalo males for meat production.
- [ ] Routine animal farm operations and labour management.
- [ ] Animal farm accounts and records.
- [ ] Methods of milking and precautions.
- [ ] Factors affecting quality and quantity of milk production.
- [ ] Clean milk production.
- [ ] Breeds of sheep and goat and their descriptions.
- [ ] Important economic traits for meat, milk and fibre.
- [ ] General management and feeding practices during different stages of growth, development and production (milk, meat and wool).
- [ ] Breeding schedule and management of ram and buck.
- [ ] Weaning and fattening of lambs and kids.

### Unit 4Zoo Animals Production Management

0 / 9

- [ ] Taxonomy of important wild zoo animals.
- [ ] Status and conservation practices of wild life in India.
- [ ] Basic principles of habitat and housing of various classes of wild zoo animals.
- [ ] Size and space requirement (dimension) of cubicles, enclosures of important wild zoo animals.
- [ ] Management of livestock in fringe areas, in and surrounding the breeding areas.
- [ ] Feeding habits, feeds and feeding schedules of captive animals.
- [ ] Restraining, capture, handling, physical examination of captive animals.
- [ ] Classification of zoos, management of sanctuaries, national parks etc. Acts and Rules related to captive animals.
- [ ] National and international organization and institutions interlinked to captive animals role and functioning.

### Unit 5Animal Welfare

0 / 19

- [ ] Definition of animal welfare and ethics.
- [ ] Human and animal welfare in relation to ecosystem and environmental factors.
- [ ] Role of veterinarians in animal welfare.
- [ ] Animal welfare organizations, Animal Welfare Board of India - their role, functions and current status.
- [ ] Rules, regulations, laws on animal welfare.
- [ ] Prevention of Cruelty to Animals (PCA) Act, 1960 {59 of 1960).
- [ ] Role and function of Committee for the Purpose of Controlling and Supervising Experiments in Animals (CPCSEA).
- [ ] Protection of wild life in nature and captivity.
- [ ] Protection and welfare of performing animals.
- [ ] Welfare of animals during transportation.
- [ ] Animal welfare in commercial livestock farming practices.
- [ ] Protection and welfare of working animals.
- [ ] Pet and companion animal welfare.
- [ ] Animal welfare during natural calamities and disaster management.
- [ ] Legal duties of veterinarians, Common offences against animals and laws related to these offences.
- [ ] Provincial and Central Acts relating to animals.
- [ ] Laws relating to offences affecting Public Health.
- [ ] Livestock Importation Act Evidence, liability and insurance.
- [ ] Code of Conduct and Ethics for veterinarians - the Regulations made under the Act.

### Unit 6Poultry Production Management

0 / 27

- [ ] Indian poultry industry — Brief outline of the different segments — poultry statistics.
- [ ] Classification of poultry with respect to production characters, age and standards.
- [ ] Production characters of other avian species.
- [ ] Description of indigenous fowls and their value in rural farming.
- [ ] Specific strains developed for rural poultry production
- [ ] their acceptability and importance in rural eco-system Brooding management — Types of brooders — preparation of shed — Importance of environmental factors.
- [ ] Housing — Types of poultry houses — space requirements.
- [ ] Recent advances in housing systems and rearing systems.
- [ ] Scavenging system of management — Low input technology — Backyard and semi-intensive units
- [ ] their management and economic achievements.
- [ ] Deep litter management — control of litter-borne diseases and recycling of litter.
- [ ] Cage management — Different types
- [ ] Advantages and disadvantages.
- [ ] Management of growers and layers.
- [ ] Management of broilers and breeders.
- [ ] Stress management.
- [ ] Feeding management—Classification of nutrients — Nutrient requirements and feed formulations.
- [ ] Feeding systems—Feed restrictions — phase feeding — Additives and supplements.
- [ ] Water management.
- [ ] Breeding systems and methods of mating.
- [ ] Selection and culling.
- [ ] Breeding for specific characters and for hybrid chicken production.
- [ ] Poultry judging.
- [ ] Egg structure — Physical and chemical composition.
- [ ] Bio-security and principles of disease prevention management.
- [ ] Health care for common poultry diseases — vaccination.
- [ ] General principles of poultry medication.

### Unit 7Diversified Poultry Production And Hatchery Management

0 / 9

- [ ] Principles of incubation and hatchery management practices.
- [ ] Factors affecting fertility and hatchability, selection and care of hatching eggs and hatchery hygiene.
- [ ] Candling, sexing, grading, packing and disposal of hatchery waste.
- [ ] Economics of hatchery business — Troubleshooting hatchery failures-Computer applications in hatchery management.
- [ ] Poultry waste management, pollution and environmental issues.
- [ ] Organic and hill farming.
- [ ] Mixed or integrated poultry farming Vertical & horizontal integration in commercial poultry production — Contract farming.
- [ ] Exportorimport of poultry produce and marketing.
- [ ] Management of ducks, geese, turkeys, Japanese quails, guinea fowls etc.

### Unit 8Laboratory Or Rabbit Or Pet Animal Production Management

0 / 15

- [ ] Importance and selection of laboratory animal, care and housing standards of mice, rats, hamster and guinea pigs.
- [ ] General considerations on feeding and breeding of laboratory animals.
- [ ] Concept of production of specific pathogen free and germ free laboratory animals.
- [ ] Scope of rabbit farming in the country, breeds and their distributions in India.
- [ ] Limitation of rabbit animal production, Selection, care and management of breeding stock for commercial purpose.
- [ ] Identification, care and management of kindling animals.
- [ ] Care of new born, growing stock.
- [ ] Breeding and selection techniques for optimal production of rabbit.
- [ ] Feeds and feeding for rabbit production.
- [ ] Hygienic care and Housing for rabbit production.
- [ ] Disposal, utilization and recycling of waste etc. Preparing projects for micro (Backyard), mini and major rabbit farms.
- [ ] Important breeds of dogs, cats and pet birds.
- [ ] Feeding of dogs, cats and pet birds.
- [ ] Dog show: preparation for show, kennel clubs, important characteristics for judgment.
- [ ] Utility of dogs- guarding, defense, patrolling, riot control, scouting, espionage, mine detection, tracking, guiding, hunting, races, retrieving rescue and other uses.

### Unit 9Swine Or Equine Or Camel, Yak And Mithun Production Management

0 / 30

- [ ] Introduction and scope of swine farming in the country.
- [ ] Demography of swine population.
- [ ] Selection and breeding techniques in swine.
- [ ] Important breeds (exotic and indigenous) & their characteristics.
- [ ] Housing and feeding of swine.
- [ ] Management of different categories of swine for optimal production: breeding and pregnant sows
- [ ] sows at farrowing and after farrowing: pig-lets, growing stock, lactating sows, feedlot stock.
- [ ] Equine population of India.
- [ ] Horses, donkeys and mules and their utility.
- [ ] Colors and markings.
- [ ] Identification of breeds of horses.
- [ ] Dentition and ageing of horses.
- [ ] Care and routine management of equines including grooming, saddling and exercise.
- [ ] Stable and its management.
- [ ] Vices of horses.
- [ ] Foot care and shoeing care.
- [ ] Feeding routine for horse, donkeys and mules.
- [ ] Care of stallion.
- [ ] Mating of horses, brood mare and its care.
- [ ] Foaling and care of newborn.
- [ ] Breeding mules.
- [ ] Care of race horses and preparing horses for show.
- [ ] Doping and its detection.
- [ ] Colic and its prevention.
- [ ] Common breeds of camel in India and their utility, peculiarities in camel.
- [ ] Feeding schedule of camel, rutting symptoms in camel, Vices of camel.
- [ ] Care of breeding in camel, pregnancy and parturition of camel.
- [ ] Population statistics and utility, peculiarities of yak.
- [ ] Feeding and breeding of MithunorYaks.
- [ ] Yak x cattle crossing, hybrids from Mithun or Yaks and their adaptation to high altitude, milk composition of Mithun or Yaks.
